title: JPMorganChase Community Outlook Survey: D.C. area residents see a city in transition – split on the economy, cutting back on dining out

# JPMorganChase Community Outlook Survey: D.C. area residents see a city in transition – split on the economy, cutting back on dining out


Nearly 4 in 10 describe the local economy as declining, while a majority report pulling back on restaurant spending in the past three months—signals of caution that are reshaping household decisions across the region


WASHINGTON, D.C.


---


November 23, 2026


Washingtonians are sending a clear message about life in the Washington area right now: they’re uncertain about where the local economy is headed and they’re adjusting their day-to-day spending accordingly. In new findings from JPMorganChase’s first-ever Community Outlook survey of the Greater D.C. area, local residents are closely split on the direction of the local economy, with 39% saying it is declining, 37% saying it is holding steady, and 29% describing their view as positive.


That uncertainty is showing up at the dinner table. More than half of D.C. residents (54%) say they have cut back on dining out in the past three months—making it the most common category for reduced spending.


“Washingtonians are telling us they want stability above all else—a sense of security that lets them plan ahead with confidence,” said Kevin Thomas, Mid-Atlantic Regional Director, Chase, and member of the Market Leadership Team, JPMorganChase. “Even where people feel uncertain about the broader economy, we help them prioritize and plan to align with long-term strategy and business goals so they’re set up for success.”


## A local economy residents are watching closely


From small business and restaurant traffic to household budgets, the survey points to a community that is actively recalibrating. More than three-quarters of D.C. residents (77%) say they follow local economic news at least somewhat closely, and many say that coverage has influenced their financial decisions, including saving more money (31%) or thinking about saving more (30%).


The spending pullback is real and it’s concentrated in everyday categories. In addition to the 54% who say they’ve cut back on dining out in recent months, residents also reported reducing spending on entertainment (43%) and travel (37%). At the same time, D.C. residents report increased spending in essential areas, led by groceries (45%) over the past year.


## What residents say they’re aiming for: stability, security, and breathing room


Even amid mixed views of the economy, residents’ goals center on long-term financial stability and near-term stress reduction. About 44% of D.C. area residents rank peace of mind and financial security among their three most important financial priorities (the most-cited goal in the market), followed by retirement and long-term savings (34%) and paying off debt (26%).


Housing remains a major factor in how residents evaluate affordability and future plans: 54% rate housing in their area as unaffordable, and 63% agree homeownership is important for financial stability.


## JPMorganChase efforts in D.C.


As part of its[American Dream Initiative,](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/american-dream-initiative-announcement) JPMorganChase is expanding its community banking efforts to help more people build the knowledge and confidence to manage their money, increasing financial health education programming with the goal of reaching 5 million people. The multi-year effort to expand economic opportunity also focuses on advancing small business growth, increasing affordable housing, improving financial health, helping people secure good jobs, expanding access to quality healthcare and strengthening local institutions in Greater Washington and communities across the country.


“These findings show a community that is clear-eyed about the pressures it faces and determined to build lasting financial security,” said Aja Clark, Community Manager in D.C. for Chase. “Our commitment in the Washington, D.C. area is to meet residents where they are with the tools, guidance, and local investments that help turn goals like saving, homeownership, and debt payoff into reality.”


JPMorganChase is working to advance an economy that works for all in Washington, D.C. by leveraging its expertise, insights, and resources to help residents, businesses, and communities achieve their goals. Across the Greater D.C. area, the firm serves more than 170,000 consumer customers, more than 15,000 small business customers and has nearly 900 employees.


Since 2021, the firm has provided about $55 million in philanthropic contributions to help strengthen local communities, increase opportunity and drive long-term economic growth in D.C.


To learn more about the firm’s impact in D.C., visit[https://www.jpmorganchase.com/communities/washington-dc](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/communities/washington-dc)


## About the survey & methodology


The Community Outlook survey was conducted by Morning Consult on behalf of JPMorganChase, measuring how residents view their financial lives, their communities, and their aspirations. Interviews were conducted online between August 24 and September 11, 2026, among a total of 7,800 U.S. adults ages 18 and older, split evenly across 13 metropolitan areas: Boston, Washington, D.C., Miami, Philadelphia, Columbus, Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas/Fort Worth, Seattle, the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, and Birmingham. Figures for Washington, D.C. reflect responses from approximately 602 residents in the Washington, D.C. metropolitan area, including Washington-Arlington-Alexandria, DC-VA-MD-WV. Results carry a margin of error of approximately ±4.0 percentage points at the 95% confidence level, and wider for subgroups. Because several cross-market differences fall within the margin of error, some readings are described as directional rather than definitive.
